Thanks for taking this on. We're in the middle of vendor onboarding in Ariba and hit two related blockers that need both legal and procurement input before we can complete registration:

1) Our legal team proposed three changes to Redwood's MSA (attached redline_msa_v2.docx) that we need to resolve before Procurement will approve the vendor record. The changes are focused on data residency, liability carve-outs for subcontractors, and an audit right clause.

2) Our Ariba portal requires PO fields to be present (GL code, remit-to identifier, and tax jurisdiction) that don't map cleanly to the order form Redwood provided. I've attached an example Ariba field spec (ariba_field_spec.xlsx) and an exported sample PO from our system.

We need a short mutual action plan: legal sign-off path for the MSA changes and confirmation from Redwood that the Order Form will populate Ariba-required fields or that we can accept exceptions. Ideally we can resolve both this week — our procurement operations team has a cutover on Monday.

Attaching: redline_msa_v2.docx, ariba_field_spec.xlsx

David / Sydney / Priyom — thanks for the context and the annotated PDF. High-level response from Redwood Legal:

- Liability carve-out: we cannot accept an open-ended carve-out for subcontractor liability. We can propose a narrowly tailored flow-down that limits liability to breach caused by Redwood-managed subprocessors and where Redwood controls contractual flow-down.
- Audit right: propose limiting to access to operational logs and only under appropriate NDA / reasonable notice; exclude intrusive on-site audits.
- Data residency: we can accept a statement of intent and a binding paragraph on where customer data is processed for Redwood-hosted deployments; for private deployments we will include the specific region commitments.

I'll circulate a short redline with alternate language by close of day today and call out anything that Procurement will need to confirm in Ariba (e.g., whether Ariba can accept a custom remit_to mapping to our billing system).

Marissa — I believe the Ariba field mapping question will be the practical gating item. If the portal cannot be extended, we should prepare an exceptions memo template for Acme procurement to sign.

-Markus
